output.brief:
The slowdown comes mainly from one change. Credit Policy v14 (effective 1 May) now requires a full inspection appraisal for property-secured loans between $150k and $500k. Before, a desktop valuation was enough. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days, against about 1.2 for desktop ones. Full appraisals rose from about 30 a month to about 80. The valuation stage for property-secured loans went from 1.6 to 8.4 days, and underwriting can't start until the report arrives. The firm's turnaround for each type hasn't changed, so the valuation firm and its contract aren't the cause. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, so Corvane isn't the main driver. Document collection is the same at the branches with new hires as elsewhere, so the new officers aren't the cause either. The policy change had no assessed impact on processing times. Its rationale is real: audit found desktop valuations ran 12% high.

What to do: take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee, and let them decide whether to amend the valuation clause. Don't withhold the Corvane payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Withdrawals are partly an artifact of the new 30-day auto-close rule, so check that before any rebate offer. I'm fairly confident in the main finding. How much the delay drives abandonment is still unproven.
